name: Marked
prompt:
In this folder, set up a small Node.js project (ES modules) that uses the marked library to render Markdown. Create `solution.mjs` that exports `renderMarkdown(markdown)`, which returns the HTML string, with two customisations done through marked's renderer or extension API (not by editing the HTML afterwards):

1. Every heading gets an `id` attribute with a slug of its text: the plain heading text (no Markdown syntax), lowercased, with every character that is not a letter, digit, space or hyphen removed, and spaces replaced by hyphens. If the same slug appears again in the same document, add `-1`, `-2` and so on to the repeats. Each call to `renderMarkdown` starts counting from scratch.
2. Links to external `http://` or `https://` URLs open in a new tab: they get `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Other links (relative paths, `#anchors`, `mailto:`) are rendered normally, without those attributes.

Everything else must render exactly as marked normally does, including inline formatting inside headings and link text, and link titles. Install the dependencies with npm.
